Preserve Eggs for a Year Without Refrigeration

Free guide — part of the Ozark Prepper library

If you keep chickens you can keep eggs for a year with a few simple, tested methods. This book covers the two safest ways: water-glassing and plain refrigeration. You learn which works, what the risks are, and exactly how to do it. Everything is written in plain English.

The two ways you will learn

  • The water-glass method: the old way. Put eggs in a jar, cover them with a special liquid, and keep them cool and dark. The liquid keeps bacteria out.
  • The plain-keep method: the modern way. Put eggs in the refrigerator, in their cartons or a covered container.

What you should know before you start

  • Only use eggs that are clean. If they are dirty, wash only what you will use right away.
  • Only use eggs that are not cracked. A cracked egg should not be preserved.
  • Only use eggs from healthy birds. An egg from a sick bird may carry germs.
  • Never eat a preserved egg that smells bad, looks odd, or has an unusual colour.
  • If it floats in water, throw it out. A fresh egg sinks. A bad one floats.

Safety first: Working with preserved food can make you very sick if you do not do it right. Read this warning twice. When in doubt, throw it out.
